title: One director exchange kernel: the live route and the simulator run the same code
acceptance: directorExchange over an in-memory store, agenda with b1 active, one candidate turn plus a begin_topic(b2) tool in the same exchange -> the stored turn event carries blockId b1 (tagged with the block active BEFORE the tool), and the returned agenda state has b2 active

body:
## Summary
Extract the director's per-exchange algorithm (persist turns tagged with the prior block, apply at most one tool, decide at most one directive, compute endCall/clock) into one pure kernel over a small event-store port. The live route wraps it in its IMMEDIATE transaction with the DB store; the simulator wraps it with an array store. The mirror, and the two source-text tests that pin it, disappear.

## Description
The simulator exists to test the REAL instrument, yet its director is a hand-kept copy of `runDirectorStep` (`director-loop.ts:3`), guarded by `engine.test.ts` grepping production source for four strings, two of them comments. That guard is both too strict (renaming a comment in the live route breaks the simulator's suite) and too loose (the copies already disagree on ackSeq and the event ceiling, and resent-turn idempotency is simply absent from the mirror). The heartbeat is the same pattern: `clock.ts` re-declares 20_000 and a regex reads `useDirector.ts` to check it. The registry's fidelity rule for a harness is that a copy must be pinned by a drift guard and that the stronger arrangement is to run the exact production path; this card takes the stronger arrangement. Afterwards a director change is made once, is exercised by both the route tests and every simulator run, and the kernel gets DB-free unit tests of its own for the first time.

## Flow
1. New `app/_lib/voice/director-exchange.ts`: `directorExchange({ agenda, attempt, attemptStartedAtMs, nowMs, turns, clientEvents, tool, store })` where `store` is `{ events(): readonly DirectorEvent[]; canStore(): boolean; append(drafts): DirectorEvent[]; maxTurnSeq(): number }`. Synchronous; no DB import.
2. `director-step.ts` keeps parsing, `touchInterviewActivity`, `clampClientAt` and `withInterviewEventsLock`, and passes a DB-backed store (ceiling, ON CONFLICT idempotency, `maxInterviewTurnSeq`).
3. `director-loop.ts` becomes an array store (with the same idempotency on (attempt, seq)) plus the kernel call; `SimExchangeResult` stays its public shape so `engine.ts` is untouched.
4. Move `DIRECTOR_HEARTBEAT_MS` into `call-observations.ts`; `useDirector.ts` and `clock.ts` import it.
5. Replace the two source-pin tests with `director-exchange.test.ts` (kernel cases + the route-vs-simulator parity sequence).
6. Update the simulator section of `docs/features/interviews/README.md` ("mirrors" -> "runs").

## Expected impact
One place to change director exchange behaviour; the simulator can no longer certify a director that production does not run; the live exchange gains DB-free unit coverage; two brittle source-text tests are retired. Everything the simulator reports (LC verdicts, the cross-block measurement, the must-ask and overrun invariants) rests on this loop, so its fidelity is the fidelity of every LC finding.

## Evaluation
Claim: the live director route and the simulator execute one exchange implementation, and their outputs agree exchange by exchange on a scripted call.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no kernel module exists; the parity test and the idempotent array store do not exist; the source pins are present).
After: 7 of 7.
Method: gate - `npm run test:unit` (new director-exchange.test.ts, engine.test.ts, director-route.test.ts), plus `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint`.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture.

title: Brief-change diff: --baseline classifies every cell fixed, regressed or noise
acceptance: diffVerdicts: baseline no_leak (reliability) pass in situation S, candidate no_leak fail in S, S and no_leak not in --targets -> cell class nonlocal_regression, report.blocking true, and the cell carries transcript refs from both sides
diffVerdicts: targets=[consent_stop]; baseline consent_stop fail, candidate pass -> intended_improvement, blocking false
diffVerdicts: baseline cell sampled 3 times with 1 fail / 3 evaluable, candidate 1 fail / 1 -> noise (inside the baseline's own spread), never nonlocal_regression
diffVerdicts: baseline pass, candidate not_evaluable (or not_provoked) -> not_comparable with that reason; it is counted in neither the regression nor the improvement totals
Cast identity: a situation whose persona text changed between the two runs (situationSha differs) -> every cell of it is not_comparable with reason 'cast changed', and the report headline names it
Both sides share briefSha and directorVersion -> the report says 'no instrument change: this is a spread measurement' and no cell can be intended_improvement
runSimulations resume: a prior dump whose situationSha differs from the current bank's persona -> the situation runs again instead of being skipped (today runner.ts:183-187 skips it)

CLI: interview-sim-verdict --runs <new> --baseline <old verdict dir> [--targets a,b] writes diff.md (non-local regressions first, then intended, noise, not comparable) and diff.json beside report.md; without --baseline nothing new is written
premise: app/_lib/interview-sim/verdict-run.ts:424-425 throws InstrumentIdentityError when dumps of one situation come from different instruments - correct for merging samples, but it leaves the operator who edited the brief NO way to compare before and after except reading two report.md files side by side

app/_lib/interview-sim/verdict-run.ts:548 already persists per-conversation verdicts (every InvariantVerdict with state, evidence seqs, instrument, providers) in verdicts.json - the baseline data exists; nothing reads it back
scripts/interview-sim-verdict.ts:71 the known flags are runs, out, judge-model, no-judge, fake-judge, characters, timeout, workers - there is no baseline, compare or targets flag

app/_lib/interview-sim/types.ts:69-82 SimConversation records situationId and the instrument (briefSha, agendaBlockIds, directorVersion) but not the situation's content, so the cast is not part of a dump's identity

app/_lib/interview-sim/runner.ts:183-187 resume skips a situation when briefSha and directorVersion match - an edited persona, firstMessage or provokes in situations.json silently reuses the stale dump
app/_lib/interview-sim/verdict-run.ts:439 evaluates every dump against the CURRENT bank (loadSituations()), so a provokes/handles edit re-grades an old transcript against a situation it never ran

Registry recruiting/conversational-assessment-validation technique prompt-change-regression-baseline: 'The question a validation run answers after a change is not did the new version pass. It is did anything that used to pass now fail'; three things pin a baseline (instrument text, the cast byte-exact, the rubric); classify every cell into intended improvement / non-local regression / non-local improvement / noise; block on any non-local reliability regression
rollback: Additive: baseline-diff.ts is new and only reached through the new --baseline flag; situationSha is an extra optional field on the dump (old dumps without it read as 'cast unknown' -> not_comparable, never a crash), and the runner's resume check gains one condition. Reverting the series restores today's behaviour exactly.
runner_up: An accept-rule rerun mode (--failing-plus-sample N): re-run only the failing situations plus a seeded random sample of passing ones after a brief edit, as the same technique's hill-climb accept rule prescribes.
body:
## Summary
Give the verdict command a compare mode. `--baseline <verdict dir>` reads the earlier run's verdicts.json and classifies every situation x invariant cell of the new run as intended improvement, non-local regression, non-local improvement, noise or not comparable, writes diff.md/diff.json, and flags a non-local reliability regression as blocking. Dumps start carrying a digest of their situation so the cast is part of the comparison's identity.

## Description
The simulator is the tuning instrument for the AI interviewer's brief and director, and the normal outcome of a brief edit is that the targeted behaviour improves while something three categories away breaks. Today the verdict run correctly refuses to MERGE two instruments (verdict-run.ts:424-425), but offers nothing to COMPARE them: the operator runs twice and reads two report.md files by eye, with no notion of which flips are real and which are the baseline's own spread. The persisted verdicts.json (verdict-run.ts:548) already holds everything a cell-by-cell diff needs. Separately, a dump does not record the situation it ran (types.ts:69-82), so an edited persona both slips past resume (runner.ts:183-187) and is re-graded against a situation it never ran (verdict-run.ts:439); the same digest closes both.

## Flow
1. `situations.ts`: `situationSha(s)` over the canonical JSON of persona, firstMessage, provokes, firstMessageProvokes, handles, fixture, language.
2. `types.ts`/`engine.ts`: `SimConversation.situationSha` written into every dump; `runner.ts` resume also requires it to match.
3. `baseline-diff.ts` (pure): `diffVerdicts(baseline, candidate, { targets })` -> cells with class, sample counts on each side, refs; `blocking` = any non-local regression on the reliability axis. Noise = the cell flipped within the baseline's own observed fail rate when the baseline has 2+ samples.
4. `verdict-run.ts`: optional `baseline` path; after the normal artifacts, load its verdicts.json, diff, write diff.json and diff.md (non-local regressions first, each with both transcripts' refs).
5. `scripts/interview-sim-verdict.ts`: `--baseline <dir>` and `--targets <invariants or situation ids>`; exit code semantics unchanged (a regression is a RESULT).
6. Document the mode in the Verdicts section of `docs/features/interviews/README.md`.

## Expected impact
Every brief or director change gets an answer to the question that matters - did anything that used to pass now fail - in one command, with noise separated from regression and the cast pinned. Turns the simulator from a snapshot reporter into a regression gate for the interviewer instrument, and stops stale dumps of edited situations from being reused or mis-graded.

## Evaluation
Claim: given two verdict runs, the tool classifies every comparable cell into the technique's four buckets plus not_comparable, marks a non-local reliability regression as blocking, and refuses to compare cells whose cast changed.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no diff module, no --baseline flag, no situationSha in dumps, resume ignores the cast).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - `npm run test:unit` (baseline-diff.test.ts, engine.test.ts resume case, verdict-run.test.ts), `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`; one keyless end-to-end on --fake runs.
Result: pending build.
Gate: none.

Registry file knowledge/recruiting/assessment/conversational-assessment-validation/techniques/prompt-change-regression-baseline.md, sections 'What a baseline is' and 'Reading a diff'.
